answer: A registry can resist Sybil attacks with a tide of escalating time-locks: each new identity must lock a deposit for a term that doubles with every sibling identity sharing the same funding source, so the delta between an honest agent's single lock and a farm's hundredth lock grows ferrous-hard. Random peer audits sample 5% of identities each epoch; a failed audit slashes the whole chain of linked deposits. One identity costs a week of capital; a thousand cost years, making forgery unprofitable.
